subject: RFI: Security telemetry — exportability, retention, and audit event schema
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@alphahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: security@alphahealth.com
Date: 2025-08-17T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Logging & telemetry exportability / retention questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking our RFI on short notice. As part of our procurement/security review I need a concise but detailed answer set to the questions below so our InfoSec and Platform teams can validate Redwood against our logging and data-retention requirements. Please include references to any attachments or sample schemas you can share.

1) What event types are produced in your platform audit logs (e.g., auth, config-change, inference request, billing, admin)?
2) For hosted Redwood, what is the default retention window for raw event logs and for aggregated/billing records?
3) Can we export logs on-demand and/or stream continuously to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/S3/Kafka)? Supported formats?
4) Does Redwood support customer-configured retention windows per-account or per-route? If so, what UI/API controls exist and what minimums/maximums apply?
5) How are PII and user-submitted content handled in logs? Any redaction/encryption options?
6) Is there a way for us to request deletion/purge of data for DSRs, and what is the SLA?
7) Are audit logs immutable/tamper-evident for compliance audits? Can you provide checksums or write-once storage options?
8) For Dedicated and Private deployments, what controls or contract options exist around retention and exportability?

We'd like answers by EOD Wednesday (2025-08-20) for inclusion in our RFP packet. If you have a short matrix or sample event schema that would be super helpful.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Director, IT Security
Alpha Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@alphahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-17T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Logging & telemetry exportability / retention questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Laura (Security & Compliance lead) and Dylan (Solutions Engineering) to provide the detailed answers and a sample schema.

Attached: a short logging/retention matrix and a sanitized example of our audit event schema (we'll follow up with the fuller JSON schema).

Laura / Dylan — could you please review the questions below and add explicit values we can share with Alpha Health? Specific asks:
- Confirm default retention windows for Hosted (raw events vs aggregated).
- Note export endpoints and formats + any operational limits (throughput, rate limits).
- Provide the event field list we can share (timestamp, request_id, user_id, model_version, tokens_in/out, latency_ms, etc.).
- Clarify redaction/encryption options and DSR purge SLA.
- State controls for Dedicated/Private (contractual retention + on-prem options).

I told Alpha we'd return an official response by EOD Wed. Happy to help with edits — I'll aggregate once you post your replies.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Answer set for Alpha Health RFI (logging + exportability)

Laura / Dylan — following up. Below I've sketched the structure we should include in the consolidated reply; please paste or paste-edit the authoritative bits. Keep answers short and declarative for the RFP.

Suggested structure (fill in where I've left placeholders):
- Event types produced (bullet list).
- Default retention (hosted): raw events = X days, aggregated/billing = Y days; retention tiers/paid extensions.
- Exportability: on-demand export (S3) / scheduled export jobs / streaming (Kafka / syslog / Splunk HEC) — include formats (NDJSON/JSON/CSV).
- Per-account retention config: API + Console UI + min/max.
- Redaction & encryption: at-rest AES-256, TLS in-flight, optional payload redaction, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Deletion/DSR: API to purge with audit trail; typical SLA = N business days.
- Immutability/tamper-evidence: internal WORM ops for Dedicated; checksums and append-only logs for compliance exports.
- Dedicated/Private notes: contractual retention up to 7 years, local storage options for Private, ability to keep logs entirely in customer VPC.

Dylan — can you attach a stripped-down JSON sample of an inference event (no PII) and a short example of the export command for S3 and Splunk? Laura — please confirm the DSR SLA and whether we can offer write-once storage for Dedicated when negotiated.

Thanks — need this back by EOD tomorrow so I can finalize.

Karthik
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@alphahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-20T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Security telemetry — exportability, retention, and audit event schema

Hi Alice — thanks for the patience. Attached are: 1) RFI_Attachment_1_Logging_Matrix.xlsx (matrix of answers), and 2) redwood-audit-schema-20250820.json (sanitized sample event schema). Below is an executive summary you can drop into the RFP; I've kept it tight but complete.

Executive summary (answers):

Event types produced
- Authentication & authorization (login_attempt, token_issue, token_revocation)
- Admin/config changes (policy_update, route_change, model_rollout, key_rotation)
- Inference requests (inference_request_received, inference_response_sent)
- System/infra (node_start, node_terminate, autoscale_event)
- Billing and usage (usage_record_generated, invoice_event)
- Security (rate_limit_triggered, anomaly_detected, suspicious_activity)

Default retention (Hosted)
- Raw event logs (line-level events, NDJSON): default 90 days.
- Aggregated/billing records (summaries used for billing & analytics): default 365 days.
- Customers can purchase extensions for Hosted (up to 3 years) as an add-on.

Exportability & streaming
- On-demand exports: export job to S3 (NDJSON or compressed NDJSON). Exports can be scheduled or triggered via API.
- Continuous streaming: supported via Kafka (plaintext or TLS), Syslog over TLS, and Splunk HEC.
- Formats: NDJSON/JSON for event-level; CSV for summarized usage reports.
- Operational notes: streaming endpoints support up to X MB/s sustained per account (we will provide rate guidance in the contract).

Per-account retention controls
- Hosted: retention window is configurable via the Redwood Console (Admin > Data retention) and via the Data Retention API. Minimum = 7 days, Maximum (self-serve) = 3 years; contract add-ons up to 7 years.
- Dedicated/Private: retention fully customer-configurable; for Private the customer elects storage location and retention policy.

PII, redaction & encryption
- In-flight: TLS 1.2+. At-rest: AES-256.
- Payloads containing user-submitted content are logged only if the customer enables full content logging; by default we log metadata and hashed prompt identifiers (prompt_hash) to reduce PII surface.
- Redaction options: configurable rules to strip or mask fields (email, ssn-like patterns) before logs are stored or exported.
- Customer-managed keys (KMS) available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Deletion / DSRs
- Customers can request object-level purge via the Data Deletion API.
- Typical SLA: Hosted purge completes within 10 business days (subject to retention tier and legal hold). Dedicated/Private purge timelines are contractual.

Immutability & tamper evidence
- Hosted: immutable export snapshots can be created for audit purposes; we provide checksums with export packages.
- Dedicated: write-once storage options and append-only logging can be enabled at contract signing for compliance needs.

Dedicated & Private notes
- Dedicated: predictably isolated storage; customers may elect extended retention policies up to 7 years (contracted).
- Private: full control of export/retention; logs may remain inside customer VPC/on-prem only.

Sample event fields (included in the attached JSON schema)
- timestamp, request_id, account_id, user_id (if available), session_id, event_type, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, node_id, region, route, prompt_hash, response_hash, error_code, raw_payload_present (true/false), redacted_fields (list).

Operational and contractual items
- Rate limits and export throughput will be documented in the SOW.
- We provide a compliance package for SOC2 reports and evidence of export/retention controls.

Next steps
- I've attached the schema and the matrix. If Alpha wants, Dylan can run a 30-minute technical review with your platform team and validate a sample streaming connection (Kafka/Splunk).

Attachments: RFI_Attachment_1_Logging_Matrix.xlsx, redwood-audit-schema-20250820.json

Please let us know if you need a formal addendum to the contract for extended retention or write-once storage options. Happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
